answers.core:
It's a core problem.
Also somewhat related to #7364.
answers.workaround:
There is not really a good workaround for this problem.
As mentioned earlier, calling `.assign` to reassign the returned array to the properly typed array is one workaround.
Additionally, this requires awareness of this problem. It is easy to miss causing an annoying error during runtime.

Another workaround involves instantiating the given type everytime the function is called to get the name using `get_class()`, but this is rather inefficient.

One could also pass another parameter to the function containing the class name as string, but this will be duplicate writing effort.
